source.title: Grokking as a Variance-Limited Phase Transition: Spectral Gating and the Epsilon-Stability Threshold

record.file_problem: None noted; the full paper text is present and readable.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests grokking on modular addition with optimizer, task-complexity, weight-decay, and noise comparisons, but uses its own spectral and variance measures rather than reproducing the original study's complete method.
record.gate_note: Results reported in the paper itself include modular-addition generalization dynamics, stability and weight-decay sweeps, and SGLD comparisons. The paper also discusses findings from cited work; those cited results are not recorded as rows. Many plotted values are described qualitatively rather than numerically.
record.test_reason: The paper trains a 2-layer MLP on modular addition with full-batch AdamW and reports delayed generalization (grokking gap peaking at P=41), regimes without a delay, a weight-decay comparison and an SGLD comparison. It uses its own spectral and variance measures rather than the original training-fraction sweep, so it bears directly on V1 and weakly on V5.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, but incomplete. The authors conclude that grokking is a conditional phase transition set by task capacity, optimizer stability (epsilon) and anisotropic noise. In their account, the delay at intermediate P is variance accumulation that lifts a spectral stability gate into a sharper generalizing basin, contrary to flat-minima views. Small P or low embedding capacity fails; large P generalizes immediately. Isotropic SGLD cannot substitute for AdamW's anisotropic rectification.
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses a 2-hidden-layer width-128 ReLU MLP on modular addition with full-batch AdamW and sweeps modulus, epsilon, weight decay, and SGLD noise. It does not reproduce the original study's full training-set-size comparison.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcome varies with task modulus/complexity, AdamW epsilon, weight decay, and whether updates use AdamW or isotropic SGLD.

fits_no_version.finding: The delay coincides with gradient variance accumulating until the AdamW stability ceiling exceeds the generalizing basin's sharpness, which is said to be 721x the initial threshold at P=41. This is described as an 'Ignition' event across P≥29.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Grokking delay under AdamW is a variance-accumulation phase gated by an edge-of-stability condition, and the generalizing basin is sharper than the memorization basin.

fits_no_version.finding: Under SGLD, Fourier sparsity stays high and the Hessian trace shows no spike, indicating no circuit formation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Isotropic noise matched in scale to AdamW does not produce circuit formation; anisotropic preconditioning is required.

fits_no_version.finding: Grokking depends on AdamW epsilon: weight norm diverges near 10^-15, generalization fails near 10^-1, and there is an optimum near 10^-4.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Grokking requires an intermediate AdamW epsilon band.

record.problems: Most reported outcomes are qualitative descriptions of figures rather than numerical values; uncertainty estimates, run counts, and seed variation are not stated. The paper does not state the training-set fraction, so its modulus sweep does not directly test the claim that smaller training sets require more optimization. The SGLD test-accuracy descriptions conflict: Figure 8 says accuracy flatlines at chance, while Section 6.1 says isotropic noise can lift accuracy above chance. The paper does not report a capability check.

untested.parts: How the delay depends on training-set size. The training fraction is never stated, so the modulus sweep cannot be mapped to dataset size.
Not tested. The paper reports no circuit-level progress measure (e.g. Fourier sparsity under AdamW over time) and no removal of memorizing components.
Not tested: no non-algorithmic data and no initialization-scale or lazy-to-rich intervention.
Not tested: no LLM pretraining or fine-tuning.
Critical dataset size, ungrokking, and a direct efficiency comparison of the generalizing and memorizing circuits.
No cross-run or cross-architecture comparison of the learned algorithm.

The epsilon sweep shows sensitivity, but there is no test of whether the delay disappears when optimizer or softmax numerical issues are controlled. High epsilon prevents generalization rather than removing the delay.

missing.what: Embedding dimension × modulus ablation: grokking requires embedding dimension roughly ≥ P, and crosses mark configurations that fail within 10^6 steps.
PCA of learned embeddings: scattered at P=17, noisy circle at P=41, clean circle at P=97. This is qualitative evidence about the learned modular-circle structure.
Isotropic noise at σ=0.01 reaches about 60–80% accuracy, above the noiseless baseline but short of perfect generalization.

record.verdict_notes: All outcome values are figure-only apart from the 721.31x sharpness ratio. No seeds, run counts or uncertainty are reported. There are internal inconsistencies: P>67 vs P≥67; the grokking regime given as 23–60 vs 29–59; SGLD at chance (Figure 8) vs 60–80% (Figure 14). If the training fraction were fixed, larger P would mean more training data, so the shrinking delay at high P could be consistent with V1's dataset-size dependence. With the fraction unstated, this cannot be determined. This is a single-author-pair preprint.

versions.untested_parts: The effect of shrinking the training set is not tested; the paper varies modulus/task complexity and does not state the training-set fraction.
The paper does not directly establish that memorizing components are removed later, or that continuous progress measures quantitatively anticipate the test-accuracy jump.
No non-algorithmic data are tested, and there is no initialization-scale or lazy-to-rich intervention.
No LLM pretraining or fine-tuning on realistic data is tested.
The paper reports a weight-decay comparison but does not test a critical dataset size or ungrokking below it, nor directly compare the efficiency of generalizing and memorizing circuits.
The paper does not compare algorithms learned across runs.
The paper varies AdamW epsilon and discusses stability, but does not test whether the reported delay disappears under controls for adaptive-optimizer instabilities or floating-point softmax limits.

All descriptions agree that near-perfect generalization is never reached within 10^6 steps.
